# On keeping a notebook

I kept a notebook for eleven years before I understood what it was for. It was not for remembering; the entries I reread are the ones I already remember. It was for slowing down. A sentence written by hand takes as long as it takes, and in that time the thought has to hold still and be looked at, which most thoughts cannot survive.

People ask how to start one and I tell them the truth: the first three are bad and you throw them away. Not literally. You keep them, and once a decade you open one and wince, as I did in 2019 with the one from 2008. But you throw away the idea that they were the thing.

There is a version of this advice that turns into a product, and I want to be careful not to give it. Nobody needs a particular pen. What matters is that the tool cannot be edited, so the sentence you wrote is the sentence you wrote, and you have to live with it long enough to see what it actually says. "The notebook does not let you hide," my friend Ines said, and she was right.
